## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Diagnose and repair the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks
are fine.

**Do not use the network.** Do not fetch code, documentation, packages,
or any other material from outside the staged workspace — diagnose and
repair using only what is staged locally.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Verdict** — healthy or unhealthy, with the evidence that decides it.
2. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
3. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
4. **Expected effect** — which metric the fix should move and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After the report is submitted, the system clears `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` and runs:

```bash
bash run_training.sh
```

This runs the workspace's `run_training.sh`, which trains with `train.py` and imports the TRL source from `/workspace/src`. The runner files `run_training.sh` and `train.py` are byte-compared against the verifier's pristine copies at grading time; modifying them fails the run. The effective configuration matches `run.py` and `train.sh`:
Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from `/workspace/model`, 256 GSM8K training questions and 64 held-out questions from `/workspace/data`,
seed 42, 2 GPU process(es), 24 optimizer steps, four completions per prompt, a 256-token completion limit,
gradient accumulation of two microbatches, and four microbatches per generation batch. W&B runs offline.
The wall-clock limit is 1,800 seconds. Model weights, reward logic, data selection and the run budget are fixed by the runner.

The verifier requires completed training, at least one nonzero gradient update, and the final held-out evaluation.
Both ranks must complete all 24 optimizer steps. Every metric the staged run reports — including the custom answer_parse_rate metric — must be reported by the fresh run at each of its generation events, computed from the data of the process that produced it; disabling a metric, or filling in a value that was not actually computed, does not satisfy this criterion.
This task evaluates optimization correctness and successful execution. Held-out correctness is reported for context and is not a calibrated performance threshold.
Only files from this fresh run are graded. Do not copy, edit or fabricate metrics.

I’ll inspect the staged code, configuration, logs, metrics, and evaluation artifacts first, then trace any suspicious behavior back to the implementation before making a minimal repair. I will avoid launching training and will write the required report once the workspace is verified.

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path
from decimal import Decimal

import numpy as np
import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TrainerCallback
from transformers.trainer_utils import get_last_checkpoint
from trl import GRPOConfig, GRPOTrainer


def number(text):
    match = re.search(r"(?:####\s*|\\boxed\{)([-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)", text)
    return format(Decimal(match.group(1).replace(",", "")).normalize(), "f") if match else None


class RecordMetrics(TrainerCallback):
    def __init__(self, directory):
        self.path = directory / f"metrics_rank{int(os.environ.get('RANK', 0))}.jsonl"

    def on_log(self, args, state, control, logs=None, **kwargs):
        with self.path.open("a") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps({"step": state.global_step, **logs}) + "\n")


class RecordedGRPO(GRPOTrainer):
    def __init__(self, *args, record_directory, record_tokens, **kwargs):
        self.record_directory = record_directory
        self.record_tokens = record_tokens
        self.record_index = 0
        self.capture_logps = False
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

    def _get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(self, *args, **kwargs):
        result = super()._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(*args, **kwargs)
        if self.capture_logps:
            self.recorded_logps = result[0].detach()
        return result

    def _compute_loss(self, model, inputs):
        self.capture_logps = self.record_tokens and model.training
        loss = super()._compute_loss(model, inputs)
        if self.capture_logps:
            directory = self.record_directory / "token_records"
            directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
            logps = self.recorded_logps
            previous = inputs.get("old_per_token_logps")
            previous = logps if previous is None else previous
            filename = f"step{self.state.global_step:04d}_batch{self.record_index:05d}_rank{self.accelerator.process_index}.npz"
            np.savez_compressed(
                directory / filename,
                logps=logps.float().cpu().numpy(),
                old_logps=previous.detach().float().cpu().numpy(),
                advantages=inputs["advantages"].detach().float().cpu().numpy(),
                mask=inputs["completion_mask"].detach().cpu().numpy(),
                generation_token_count=float(inputs["num_items_in_batch"]),
                loss=float(loss.detach()),
                accumulation_steps=self.current_gradient_accumulation_steps,
                generation_steps=self.args.steps_per_generation,
                world_size=self.accelerator.num_processes,
                clip_low=self.epsilon_low,
                clip_high=self.epsilon_high,
            )
            self.record_index += 1
        self.capture_logps = False
        return loss


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--data", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--case", choices=["tokens", "metrics"], required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=24)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rank = int(os.environ.get("RANK", 0))
    rollout_path = args.output / f"rollouts_rank{rank}.jsonl"
    dataset = Dataset.from_parquet(str(args.data / "train.parquet")).shuffle(seed=args.seed).select(range(256))
    validation = Dataset.from_parquet(str(args.data / "test.parquet")).select(range(64))

    def format_row(row):
        return {"prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": row["question"] + "\nSolve the problem and write the final numerical answer after ####."}], "answer": number(row["answer"])}

    dataset = dataset.map(format_row, remove_columns=dataset.column_names)
    validation = validation.map(format_row, remove_columns=validation.column_names)

    def correctness(completions, answer, prompts, log_metric, trainer_state, **kwargs):
        texts = [completion[0]["content"] for completion in completions]
        parsed = [number(text) for text in texts]
        rewards = [float(predicted == expected) for predicted, expected in zip(parsed, answer)]
        with rollout_path.open("a") as stream:
            for prompt, text, expected, predicted, reward in zip(prompts, texts, answer, parsed, rewards):
                stream.write(json.dumps({"step": trainer_state.global_step, "prompt": prompt, "completion": text, "answer": expected, "parsed": predicted, "reward": reward}) + "\n")
        if args.case == "metrics" and rank == 0:
            log_metric("answer_parse_rate", sum(value is not None for value in parsed) / len(parsed))
        return rewards

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True, padding_side="left")
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="sdpa")
    configuration = GRPOConfig(
        output_dir=str(args.output / "checkpoints"),
        run_name=f"gsm8k_{args.case}_seed{args.seed}",
        max_steps=args.steps,
        seed=args.seed,
        data_seed=args.seed,
        per_device_train_batch_size=2,
        per_device_eval_batch_size=4,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=2,
        steps_per_generation=4,
        num_generations=4,
        max_completion_length=256,
        temperature=0.8,
        learning_rate=1e-6,
        lr_scheduler_type="constant",
        bf16=True,
        beta=0.0,
        loss_type="dapo",
        scale_rewards="group",
        use_vllm=False,
        use_liger_kernel=False,
        gradient_checkpointing=False,
        logging_steps=1,
        save_strategy="steps",
        save_steps=6,
        save_total_limit=1,
        eval_strategy="no",
        report_to=["wandb"],
        ddp_timeout=90,
        ddp_find_unused_parameters=False,
    )
    trainer = RecordedGRPO(
        model=model,
        processing_class=tokenizer,
        args=configuration,
        train_dataset=dataset,
        eval_dataset=validation,
        reward_funcs=correctness,
        record_directory=args.output,
        record_tokens=args.case == "tokens",
        callbacks=[RecordMetrics(args.output)],
    )
    checkpoint = get_last_checkpoint(str(args.output / "checkpoints")) if args.resume else None
    result = trainer.train(resume_from_checkpoint=checkpoint)
    trainer.save_state()
    metrics = trainer.evaluate()
    if trainer.accelerator.is_main_process:

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path
from decimal import Decimal

import numpy as np
import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TrainerCallback
from transformers.trainer_utils import get_last_checkpoint
from trl import GRPOConfig, GRPOTrainer


def number(text):
    match = re.search(r"(?:####\s*|\\boxed\{)([-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)", text)
    return format(Decimal(match.group(1).replace(",", "")).normalize(), "f") if match else None


class RecordMetrics(TrainerCallback):
    def __init__(self, directory):
        self.path = directory / f"metrics_rank{int(os.environ.get('RANK', 0))}.jsonl"

    def on_log(self, args, state, control, logs=None, **kwargs):
        with self.path.open("a") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps({"step": state.global_step, **logs}) + "\n")


class RecordedGRPO(GRPOTrainer):
    def __init__(self, *args, record_directory, record_tokens, **kwargs):
        self.record_directory = record_directory
        self.record_tokens = record_tokens
        self.record_index = 0
        self.capture_logps = False
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

    def _get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(self, *args, **kwargs):
        result = super()._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(*args, **kwargs)
        if self.capture_logps:
            self.recorded_logps = result[0].detach()
        return result

    def _compute_loss(self, model, inputs):
        self.capture_logps = self.record_tokens and model.training
        loss = super()._compute_loss(model, inputs)
        if self.capture_logps:
            directory = self.record_directory / "token_records"
            directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
            logps = self.recorded_logps
            previous = inputs.get("old_per_token_logps")
            previous = logps if previous is None else previous
            filename = f"step{self.state.global_step:04d}_batch{self.record_index:05d}_rank{self.accelerator.process_index}.npz"
            np.savez_compressed(
                directory / filename,
                logps=logps.float().cpu().numpy(),
                old_logps=previous.detach().float().cpu().numpy(),
                advantages=inputs["advantages"].detach().float().cpu().numpy(),
                mask=inputs["completion_mask"].detach().cpu().numpy(),
                generation_token_count=float(inputs["num_items_in_batch"]),
                loss=float(loss.detach()),
                accumulation_steps=self.current_gradient_accumulation_steps,
                generation_steps=self.args.steps_per_generation,
                world_size=self.accelerator.num_processes,
                clip_low=self.epsilon_low,
                clip_high=self.epsilon_high,
            )
            self.record_index += 1
        self.capture_logps = False
        return loss


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--data", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--case", choices=["tokens", "metrics"], required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=24)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rank = int(os.environ.get("RANK", 0))
    rollout_path = args.output / f"rollouts_rank{rank}.jsonl"
    dataset = Dataset.from_parquet(str(args.data / "train.parquet")).shuffle(seed=args.seed).select(range(256))
    validation = Dataset.from_parquet(str(args.data / "test.parquet")).select(range(64))

    def format_row(row):
        return {"prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": row["question"] + "\nSolve the problem and write the final numerical answer after ####."}], "answer": number(row["answer"])}

    dataset = dataset.map(format_row, remove_columns=dataset.column_names)
    validation = validation.map(format_row, remove_columns=validation.column_names)

    def correctness(completions, answer, prompts, log_metric, trainer_state, **kwargs):
        texts = [completion[0]["content"] for completion in completions]
        parsed = [number(text) for text in texts]
        rewards = [float(predicted == expected) for predicted, expected in zip(parsed, answer)]
        with rollout_path.open("a") as stream:
            for prompt, text, expected, predicted, reward in zip(prompts, texts, answer, parsed, rewards):
                stream.write(json.dumps({"step": trainer_state.global_step, "prompt": prompt, "completion": text, "answer": expected, "parsed": predicted, "reward": reward}) + "\n")
        if args.case == "metrics" and rank == 0:
            log_metric("answer_parse_rate", sum(value is not None for value in parsed) / len(parsed))
        return rewards

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True, padding_side="left")
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="sdpa")
    configuration = GRPOConfig(
        output_dir=str(args.output / "checkpoints"),
        run_name=f"gsm8k_{args.case}_seed{args.seed}",
        max_steps=args.steps,
        seed=args.seed,
        data_seed=args.seed,
        per_device_train_batch_size=2,
        per_device_eval_batch_size=4,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=2,
        steps_per_generation=4,
        num_generations=4,
        max_completion_length=256,
        temperature=0.8,
        learning_rate=1e-6,
        lr_scheduler_type="constant",
        bf16=True,
        beta=0.0,
        loss_type="dapo",
        scale_rewards="group",
        use_vllm=False,
        use_liger_kernel=False,
        gradient_checkpointing=False,
        logging_steps=1,
        save_strategy="steps",
        save_steps=6,
        save_total_limit=1,
        eval_strategy="no",
        report_to=["wandb"],
        ddp_timeout=90,
        ddp_find_unused_parameters=False,
    )
    trainer = RecordedGRPO(
        model=model,
        processing_class=tokenizer,
        args=configuration,
        train_dataset=dataset,
        eval_dataset=validation,
        reward_funcs=correctness,
        record_directory=args.output,
        record_tokens=args.case == "tokens",
        callbacks=[RecordMetrics(args.output)],
    )
    checkpoint = get_last_checkpoint(str(args.output / "checkpoints")) if args.resume else None
    result = trainer.train(resume_from_checkpoint=checkpoint)
    trainer.save_state()
    metrics = trainer.evaluate()
    if trainer.accelerator.is_main_process:
        (args.output / "final_metrics.json").write_text(json.dumps({"step": trainer.state.global_step, "training": result.metrics, "evaluation": metrics}, indent=2) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    def _prepare_inputs(self, generation_batch: dict[str, torch.Tensor | Any]) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor | Any]:
        # Prepares inputs for model training/evaluation by managing completion generation and batch handling.
        # During training:
        #   - Receives the local generation batch (Per-GPU batch size × steps per generation)
        #     from the modified training dataloader instead of the standard local batch
        #   - Generates completions once for the entire generation batch and splits it into batches of size
        #     `per_device_train_batch_size`
        #   - Buffers these completions and returns the appropriate slice for the current accumulation step
        #   - Optimizes by regenerating completions only periodically (every steps_per_generation * num_iterations)
        # During evaluation:
        #   - The input is treated as a standard local batch (no accumulation, no multiple iterations)
        #   - Completions are generated for each batch without buffering or reuse
        # Returns a single local batch in both cases.

        mode = "train" if self.model.training else "eval"
        if mode == "train":
            generate_every = self.args.steps_per_generation * self.num_iterations
            if self._step % generate_every == 0 or self._buffered_inputs is None:
                # self._buffered_inputs=None can occur when resuming from a checkpoint
                generation_batch = self._generate_and_score_completions(generation_batch)
                generation_batch = split_pixel_values_by_grid(generation_batch)
                generation_batch = shuffle_sequence_dict(generation_batch)
                generation_batches = split_tensor_dict(generation_batch, self.args.steps_per_generation)
                self._buffered_inputs = [unsplit_pixel_values_by_grid(batch) for batch in generation_batches]
            inputs = self._buffered_inputs[self._step % self.args.steps_per_generation]
        else:
            # In evaluation, there is neither batch grouping for generation, nor multiple iterations, hence
            # local generation batch == local eval batch
            inputs = self._generate_and_score_completions(generation_batch)
        return inputs

    def _log_metric(self, name: str, value: float):
        """
        Log a scalar metric from a reward function. Called via the `log_metric` kwarg. Values are averaged over each
        logging step and reported alongside built-in metrics like `kl` and `entropy`.

        Args:
            name (`str`):
                Name of the metric.
            value (`float`):
                Scalar value for this batch.
        """
        self._pending_metrics[name].append(value)

    def _generate_and_score_completions(
        self, inputs: list[dict[str, torch.Tensor | Any]]
    ) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor | Any]:
        device = self.accelerator.device
        mode = "train" if self.model.training else "eval"

        # `prompt` is optional only when an environment owns the data (e.g. a multi-environment routing dataset that
        # carries only an `environment` column); each rollout's `reset()` then supplies it. Default it here rather than
        # writing it back onto the row, so the placeholder stays out of the `reset()` kwargs built below, while every
        # prompt-derived check downstream (conversational detection, multimodal handling) stays consistent. Without an
        # environment, a missing `prompt` is a malformed dataset and must still fail fast.
        if self.environment_factories is not None:
            prompts = [x.get("prompt", [{"role": "user", "content": ""}]) for x in inputs]
        else:
            prompts = [x["prompt"] for x in inputs]

        # Resolve each example's environment and draw one reusable instance per rollout from the pool, creating more
        # only when this batch needs more concurrent instances of an environment than exist. `_batch_environments`
        # records each example's environment so `_tokenize_prompts` can render the matching tool schema.
        if self.environment_factories is not None:
            self._batch_environments = [x.get("environment") if self._multi_environment else None for x in inputs]
            if self._multi_environment:
                for name in set(self._batch_environments):
                    if name not in self.environment_factories:
                        raise ValueError(
                            f"Example has `environment={name!r}`, which is not among the environments passed to "
                            f"`environment_factory`. Expected one of: {list(self.environment_factories)}."
                        )
            self.environments = []
            pool_cursor = {}  # how many instances of each environment have been handed out so far this batch
            for name in self._batch_environments:
                pool = self._environment_pool[name]
                index = pool_cursor.get(name, 0)
                if index == len(pool):
                    pool.append(self.environment_factories[name]())
                pool_cursor[name] = index + 1
                self.environments.append(pool[index])

        # its environment. Done here (not at init) because each example's environment, hence its tools, is data-dependent.

                        if member_name not in ("reset", "get_reward") and not member_name.startswith("_")

"""Reproduce the staged collective mismatch and validate the patched metric flush.

Mirrors GRPOTrainer._generate_and_score_completions' `_pending_metrics` flush: run.py's reward
function calls log_metric on rank 0 only, so rank 1's pending dict is empty.
"""

import os
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import timedelta

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from accelerate import Accelerator, InitProcessGroupKwargs
from accelerate.utils import gather_object

os.environ.setdefault("ACCELERATE_USE_CPU", "true")

MODE = sys.argv[1]


def old_flush(accelerator, pending, device, metrics):
    """Pre-patch: iterate over locally pending names, collective inside the loop."""
    calls = 0
    for name in sorted(pending):
        values = pending[name]
        local_mean = sum(values) / len(values)
        metrics[name].append(accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).mean().item())
        calls += 1
    pending.clear()
    return calls


def new_flush(accelerator, pending, device, metrics):
    """Patched: agree on the name union collectively, then one gather per name on every rank."""
    calls = 0
    for name in sorted(set(gather_object(sorted(pending)))):
        values = pending.get(name, [])
        local_mean = sum(values) / len(values) if values else float("nan")
        metrics[name].append(accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).nanmean().item())
        calls += 1
    pending.clear()
    return calls


def main():
    dist.init_process_group(backend="gloo", timeout=timedelta(seconds=30))
    accelerator = Accelerator(cpu=True, kwargs_handlers=[InitProcessGroupKwargs(timeout=timedelta(seconds=30))])
    rank = accelerator.process_index
    device = accelerator.device

    # Sanity: confirm gather_object really is collective here, otherwise the test proves nothing.
    probe = gather_object([f"r{rank}"])
    print(f"[rank{rank}] probe={probe} world={accelerator.num_processes}", flush=True)
    assert sorted(probe) == ["r0", "r1"], f"gather_object not collective: {probe}"

    flush = old_flush if MODE == "old" else new_flush
    metrics = defaultdict(list)
    total_calls = 0

    for event, value in enumerate([0.5, 1.0]):
        # run.py logs `answer_parse_rate` from rank 0 only.
        pending = defaultdict(list)
        if rank == 0:
            pending["answer_parse_rate"].append(value)
        total_calls += flush(accelerator, pending, device, metrics)

    # Every rank must issue the same number of collectives, or NCCL desynchronizes.
    counts = gather_object([total_calls])
    print(f"[rank{rank}] {MODE}: gather_calls={total_calls} all_counts={counts} metrics={dict(metrics)}", flush=True)

    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Reproduce the staged collective mismatch and validate the patched metric flush.

Mirrors GRPOTrainer._generate_and_score_completions' `_pending_metrics` flush: run.py's reward
function calls log_metric on rank 0 only, so rank 1's pending dict is empty.
"""

import os
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import timedelta

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from accelerate import Accelerator, InitProcessGroupKwargs
from accelerate.utils import gather_object

os.environ.setdefault("ACCELERATE_USE_CPU", "true")

MODE = sys.argv[1]


def old_flush(accelerator, pending, device, metrics):
    """Pre-patch: iterate over locally pending names, collective inside the loop."""
    calls = 0
    for name in sorted(pending):
        values = pending[name]
        local_mean = sum(values) / len(values)
        metrics[name].append(accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).mean().item())
        calls += 1
    pending.clear()
    return calls


def new_flush(accelerator, pending, device, metrics):
    """Patched: agree on the name union collectively, then one gather per name on every rank."""
    calls = 0
    for name in sorted(set(gather_object(sorted(pending)))):
        values = pending.get(name, [])
        local_mean = sum(values) / len(values) if values else float("nan")
        metrics[name].append(accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).nanmean().item())
        calls += 1
    pending.clear()
    return calls


def main():
    dist.init_process_group(backend="gloo", timeout=timedelta(seconds=30))
    accelerator = Accelerator(cpu=True, kwargs_handlers=[InitProcessGroupKwargs(timeout=timedelta(seconds=30))])
    rank = accelerator.process_index
    device = accelerator.device

    # Sanity: confirm gather_object really is collective here, otherwise the test proves nothing.
    probe = gather_object([f"r{rank}"])
    print(f"[rank{rank}] probe={probe} world={accelerator.num_processes}", flush=True)
    assert sorted(probe) == ["r0", "r1"], f"gather_object not collective: {probe}"

    flush = old_flush if MODE == "old" else new_flush
    metrics = defaultdict(list)
    total_calls = 0

    for event, value in enumerate([0.5, 1.0]):
        # run.py logs `answer_parse_rate` from rank 0 only.
        pending = defaultdict(list)
        if rank == 0:
            pending["answer_parse_rate"].append(value)
        total_calls += flush(accelerator, pending, device, metrics)

    # Every rank must issue the same number of collectives, or NCCL desynchronizes.
    counts = gather_object([total_calls])
    print(f"[rank{rank}] {MODE}: gather_calls={total_calls} all_counts={counts} metrics={dict(metrics)}", flush=True)

    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

steps.message: The causal defect is now isolated: `train.py` intentionally logs `answer_parse_rate` only on rank 0, while the staged GRPO flush loops over each rank’s local metric names. Rank 0 therefore enters `accelerator.gather()` and rank 1 skips it, producing the exact broadcast/all-gather mismatch in the log. I’ll repair the trainer to agree on the union of metric names first, use `NaN` for a rank that did not produce that metric, and aggregate with `nanmean` so no value is fabricated.

+        # Flush user-logged metrics (from log_metric), averaging across processes. Reward functions may log a
+        # metric on only the process that has the relevant data. Agree on the metric-name union first so every rank
+        # executes the same collectives, and use NaN on ranks without a local value so the aggregate is computed only
+        # from processes that actually produced the metric.
+        metric_names = sorted(set(gather_object(sorted(self._pending_metrics))))
+        for name in metric_names:
+            values = self._pending_metrics.get(name, [])
+            local_mean = sum(values) / len(values) if values else float("nan")
+            global_mean = self.accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).nanmean().item()
             self._metrics[mode][name].append(global_mean)
*** End Patch";
